title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-7
notes:
West leads the ♣5 against 3♠. South wins the opening club lead in the dummy and must avoid losing 3 heart tricks. South has 2 certain diamond losers. If South has to play hearts himself, he is likely to lose 3 tricks in the suit.

If spades are 2-2, South can arrange to have the defense play hearts for him. South will then be guaranteed to lose only 2 heart tricks. South should ruff a club at trick 2 to prepare for an elimination. South next cashes 2 rounds of spades ending in the dummy. When both defenders follow, South is home. South cashes the ♣K for a diamond discard and ruffs dummy's last club.

South exits a diamond. The defense wins and can cash another diamond trick, but they must then break hearts or lead a diamond, conceding a ruff and discard. In either case South loses only 2 heart tricks.
